title: Pilot explicit state with and without retained coding history
hypothesis: Replacing history after each tool batch with bounded explicit state and the latest observation preserves short coding-task correctness while reducing total inference cost versus normal LCA and explicit state plus history.
falsified_if: State-only repeatedly loses constraints, acts on contradicted beliefs, repeats resolved investigations, or loses deterministic correctness; or retained history plus identical state consistently performs better. This pilot cannot establish the long-task hypothesis.
local_evidence: User-proposed state-machine hypothesis, 2026-09-05. Existing ambiguous bug and multifile coding trajectories have medians of 11 and 14 tool calls, so this is an activation and overhead pilot only.
deterministic_outcomes: external scenario hard gates and pass rate
state emitted on every response within 8000 bytes
state-only requests contain original user instructions, current state and only latest batch, without older provider reasoning
manual trajectory review of stale beliefs and repeated investigations
efficiency_outcomes: all-run estimated API cost including state output and failed responses
prompt, cached, uncached and output tokens
decision_rule: Run three randomized repetitions per scenario and arm (54 runs). Missing/invalid state is a protocol failure, with no silent fallback or extra retry. Audit exact requests before interpreting results. Continue to longer-task construction only if all state-only hard gates pass and no repeated memory-loss pattern appears. Reject this implementation on repeatable correctness losses; revise the protocol only as a new experiment. Cost reduction of at least 20% and median latency within +10% relative to normal is a promising efficiency signal, not an adoption criterion on these short tasks. Mixed or small-sample outcomes are inconclusive. C isolates the effect of keeping history under the same state requirement. Context-boundary scenario tests user corrections with existing default limits; this pilot does not force compaction or claim a real long context boundary. No production default changes.
